report.source_text: The culture after 5 days showed radiated powdery colonies of khaki yellow color (Figure 1). Direct examination of the colony showed terminal and intercalary chlamydospores (Figure 2). Faced with the difficulty of morphological identification, a real-time PCR was performed using the DermaGenius® 2.0 kit (PathoNostics, the Netherlands). Data analysis was performed using the 2nd-derivative and Tm-calling function of the LC480 software (version 1.5.1.62 SP2). This allowed the identification of Epidermophyton floccosum (Figure 3).

report.source_text: a mycological sampling on the Toe web spaces and soles of feet was carried out. Direct examination objectified mycelial filaments.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 70-year-old patient with diabetes and rheumatoid arthritis on tocilizumab presented with fever, painful swelling, and an erythematous plaque on the right leg, along with scaly plantar keratoderma and intertrigo of toe web spaces. Mycological sampling (skin scraping) was performed, and direct examination revealed mycelial filaments. Fungal culture after 5 days showed characteristic colonies, and real-time PCR identified Epidermophyton floccosum. The patient was initially treated with amoxicillin/clavulanic acid and topical terbinafine, and subsequently started on oral terbinafine 250 mg daily for 6 months (ongoing treatment).

key_supporting_evidence.claim: Patient presented with clinical signs suggestive of both bacterial and fungal infection, including fever, painful swelling, erythematous plaque on the leg, scaly plantar keratoderma, and intertrigo of toe web spaces.
Direct examination of mycological sampling (skin scraping) revealed mycelial filaments.
Fungal culture after 5 days showed radiated powdery colonies of khaki yellow color, and direct examination of the colony showed terminal and intercalary chlamydospores.
Real-time PCR performed on the fungal culture identified Epidermophyton floccosum.
Initial treatment included amoxicillin and clavulanic acid, and terbinafine ointment twice daily.
Patient was subsequently put on oral terbinafine 250 mg daily for 6 months, which was ongoing treatment.
